title: Glow parts with MeshBasicMaterial don't count as support (lamp tops 'float')
summary: The contact check skips all-MeshBasicMaterial meshes (effects), so a lantern top on a basic glow 'floats 16 cm'. Use an emissive MeshStandardMaterial for load-bearing glowing parts.

versions.note: seed harvest of the shot-match scenes (L3)

usage.example: new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x000000, emissive: 0xffd090, emissiveIntensity: 1, toneMapped: false })   // looks like a basic glow, counts as solid

doc.when: A glowing part carries something (lantern glass under a cap, a lit panel holding a frame).

problem.symptom: FLOATING for a lamp/lantern part that sits on a glowing piece.
problem.cause: lib/contact.js ignores meshes whose materials are all MeshBasicMaterial.
problem.fix: Emissive MeshStandardMaterial (color black, toneMapped false) for the glowing support.
problem.detect: The floating part's support is a glow mesh.
